nodes.label: Fidelity
nodes.rationale: Stored with the facts it describes and never recomputed at query time, because it reports the analysis that ran rather than the machine as it is now. Held per file rather than per repository, and never read as a completeness claim: a typed file may still have blind spots.

nodes.label: Precondition
nodes.rationale: An unmet precondition lowers fidelity rather than failing the run, so an unprepared repository still gets an answer.

nodes.label: Remediation
nodes.rationale: codedocs reports the command that would clear a precondition but never runs it, keeping the tool read-only over the user's repository.

nodes.label: Provenance
nodes.rationale: Three values — deterministic, syntactic, inferred — carried by the fact itself rather than attached when rendering, so trust survives every renderer.

nodes.label: Blind spot
nodes.rationale: Named concretely and per answer rather than summarised as a score, because a score cannot tell the caller what was missed.

nodes.label: Completeness
nodes.rationale: A binary property of one answer — complete, or it names its blind spots — deliberately not a percentage.

nodes.label: Preflight
nodes.rationale: Signals 1-3 run first and unconditionally because they cost microseconds; the fourth signal falls out of extraction. A type checker's diagnostics are rejected as a signal because they cost 3,100x the specifier scan and cannot distinguish a prepared repository from an unprepared one.

nodes.label: Environment fingerprint
nodes.rationale: Lockfile hash, compilerOptions and the count plus set-hash of globbed files — none of which walks node_modules, so a hand-modified install under an unchanged lockfile reads as unchanged. That is the accepted blind spot, and what doctor --measure exists for.

nodes.label: Unresolved specifier
nodes.rationale: Recorded as a fact with one of four causes rather than dropped or reduced to a ratio. Reported deduplicated per distinct specifier because one absent generated artefact produced 302 sites on cal.com. unmapped and broken carry no remediation: none would help, and none is a command.

nodes.label: Node
nodes.rationale: Five kinds only — Package, Project, File, Symbol, Document. A Repository is the index header, not a node.

nodes.label: Edge
nodes.rationale: A closed set of nine kinds. What PRD §25 calls a Relationship is the edge set, never a node alongside File.

nodes.label: SymbolId
nodes.rationale: A SCIP symbol string in codedocs' own scheme, with the workspace package version normalised away. Deterministic and scoped to one snapshot: it says what a symbol is called at this commit and nothing about the past.

nodes.label: Descriptor path
nodes.rationale: One segment per scope, taken from what the author wrote, so a SymbolId survives a sibling being inserted above it where an ordinal would not.

nodes.label: Collision
nodes.rationale: Counted on the symbol and named as a blind spot by any operation walking its edges, because the answer really is their union. Distinct from the deliberate collapse of overloads and declaration merging, which are one symbol.

nodes.label: Durable
nodes.rationale: Local symbols are not durable and nothing durable may anchor to one, so documents and impact baselines cannot be pinned to an id that will not survive an edit. No durable id collides.

nodes.label: Derivation
nodes.rationale: Named on the fact itself, in order of strength, so an inferred fact is actionable rather than merely hedged.

nodes.label: Continuity
nodes.rationale: Kept as a separate inferred layer and never a property of the SymbolId, because no existing system has managed to make identity survive a rename. Two matchers: subject matching needs no baseline; snapshot matching is only what impact needs.

nodes.label: Candidate
nodes.rationale: Ranked by evidence rather than by a score, and never asserted as the answer even when alone in the list. An empty list means no candidate was found, never that the subject was deleted.

nodes.label: Label
nodes.rationale: The third kind of thing the index holds, keyed by node id so it labels a Symbol as readily as a File — never a node itself.

nodes.label: Role
nodes.rationale: Helpers, mocks and fixtures are test rather than a role of their own, because everything that excludes tests wants them excluded too.

nodes.label: Authorship
nodes.rationale: Orthogonal to Role, because generated code is still source and a config file is still authored. Distinct from Provenance, which is about a fact rather than a file.

nodes.label: Project
nodes.rationale: One tsconfig and the files it globs. A file may belong to several; one of them is canonical. What fidelity and the environment fingerprint are held against.

nodes.label: Export-shape hash
nodes.rationale: Gates incremental propagation: a file whose content changed but whose export shape did not stops the wave.

nodes.label: Shape hash
nodes.rationale: The per-symbol version, expanded structurally for type-ish symbols, which is what makes a move detectable — same shape, same descriptor suffix, different path.

nodes.label: Caller attribution
nodes.rationale: The walk seeks the nearest callable ancestor first and only credits a variable where there is none, because stopping at the nearest named declaration credits a hook's calls to the constant holding its result. Module-level and anonymous-callback calls go to the file — the honest answer, not a dropped edge.

nodes.label: Unresolved call
nodes.rationale: Stored as a fact with one of three causes rather than dropped. dynamic is the one cause where codedocs cannot know what it missed.

nodes.label: Index
nodes.rationale: A derived artifact: never committed, always safe to delete.

nodes.label: Snapshot
nodes.rationale: A commit plus whatever is uncommitted on top of it. One index holds exactly one, which is what makes a SymbolId snapshot-scoped.

nodes.label: Drift
nodes.rationale: Detected before every answer and either repaired or named. A file counts as new against the previous tree walk rather than against the files analysed, so a source file no project globs never reads as newly appeared.

nodes.label: Baseline
nodes.rationale: Immutable once written, never part of the live index and never moved to another machine; nothing not durable may anchor to one.

nodes.label: Capture
nodes.rationale: Happens as a side effect of an analysis over a clean working tree, never as a command of its own.

nodes.label: Baseline substitution
nodes.rationale: Part of an answer's scope, reported with the commit requested, the commit used and the distance between them — never a blind spot.

nodes.label: Document
nodes.rationale: Found by scanning for claims rather than by living in a particular directory, and committed unlike the index.

nodes.label: Claim
nodes.rationale: Drawn from a closed set of predicates and anchored to a durable subject. An assertion no predicate can express is not a claim and is not checked.

nodes.label: Verdict
nodes.rationale: Four values, each with exactly one source; provenance is reported alongside a verdict, never as a fifth one.

nodes.label: Claim coverage
nodes.rationale: Reported with every verdict so verified cannot be read as "all of this is true". Distinct from completeness and never combined with it into a score.

nodes.label: Operation
nodes.rationale: The unit the whole product is built from. CLI, --json and the MCP server are renderers or bindings of the same operation, one to one — nothing composes operations above them.

nodes.label: Renderer
nodes.rationale: The human renderer is a pure function of the envelope: it may group, colour and page, never re-sort or withhold silently.

nodes.label: Envelope
nodes.rationale: One fixed wrapper for every answer, and a failure is the same envelope carrying an error, so a parser never meets a second shape.

nodes.label: Truncation
nodes.rationale: Distinct from a blind spot: codedocs knows exactly what it withheld, and reports how many exist.

nodes.label: Scope
nodes.rationale: Echoed with every answer as an excluded count, never as a blind spot or truncation, because it is part of the question rather than a limit on the answer.

nodes.label: Path
nodes.rationale: trace's result unit, carrying why it stopped. Steps are grouped by callee rather than by call site, so two calls between the same pair are one step with two sites and not two paths.

nodes.label: Evidence
nodes.rationale: Everything the index holds about one subject, assembled for someone else to write prose from. What PRD §9's explain becomes once codedocs never generates text.

nodes.label: codedocs (local TypeScript codebase index)
nodes.rationale: Indexes the whole repository into one SQLite file beside the working tree so it can answer cross-repository questions an editor cannot.

nodes.label: No LLM principle
nodes.rationale: codedocs emits deterministic structured facts and the calling agent writes the prose, so there is no provider, no API key and no inference cost anywhere in it.

nodes.label: The CLI is the product
nodes.rationale: Every operation has a human renderer and a --json renderer over one fixed envelope; agents consume it by shelling out, the way this repo already uses graphify and fallow.

nodes.label: analyse operation
nodes.rationale: Every question repairs the index before answering, so analyse exists only so a cold build in CI can be a step that fails on its own rather than a hidden cost inside the first question.

nodes.label: symbol operation
nodes.rationale: The only operation taking a glob, and it never ranks: a ranking is a judgement, and a judgement cannot also be the guarantee that the same commit gives the same answer.

nodes.label: callers operation
nodes.rationale: Returns one row per call site, not per caller, and follows calls through barrel files and renamed re-exports to the real declaration.

nodes.label: trace operation
nodes.rationale: Unbounded unless bounded with --depth, because only a quarter of a repository's call sites stay inside it, so a walk meets node_modules long before combinatorics. Cycles terminate and are marked; a depth-cut branch says so, so a bounded answer cannot be read as a whole one.

nodes.label: Ambiguous subject is not an error
nodes.rationale: The answer covers every symbol the name matched and the envelope names them, because making the caller ask again costs a round trip to learn something the answer already contains.

nodes.label: --json is explicit and unbounded by default
nodes.source_location: For agents: one envelope, every answer
nodes.rationale: Never inferred from a TTY, because sniffing a pipe makes the same command behave differently depending on where it runs — and a capped answer an agent reads as whole is a wrong answer with a footnote. --limit's default belongs to the renderer, not the operation.

nodes.label: codedocs mcp server
nodes.rationale: The tool list is derived from the same manifest the CLI parser reads and a call is answered by handing an argv to the function codedocs itself calls, so the bytes are the --json bytes by construction. mcp is not an operation: it owes no envelope and appears in no tool list.

nodes.label: .codedocs/index.db
nodes.rationale: Not committed: it is binary so git cannot delta it, and six commits of about a hundred rows grew .git by 25 MB. It writes its own .gitignore so git status stays clean, and deleting the directory is the supported way to force a cold build.

nodes.label: Incremental repair
nodes.rationale: Drift is detected by stat and a tree walk rather than git status — faster, and it sees the untracked files a tsconfig globs that git does not, so a branch switch, a rebase and a dirty tree are all just changed signatures. Propagation reaches direct importers only, gated on the exported shape.

nodes.label: Exit code convention
nodes.rationale: 0 answered, 1 a negative finding, 2 could not answer — borrowed from fallow. Nothing produces 1 yet; ADR 0006 assigns it to docs check finding a contradicted claim and doctor finding an unmet precondition.

nodes.label: cal.com benchmark
nodes.rationale: 4,827 files across 28 TypeScript projects at commit 176037d: 17 s cold build to 48,069 symbols and 26,091 call edges, 0.8 s one-file repair, ~0.3 s warm question, 17 MB on disk. Every performance claim in the README is measured against fixture repositories in repos/.

nodes.label: codedocs.jsonc config (planned)
nodes.rationale: So a repository can name projects discovery misses — plus a rule about what is allowed to enter it. Issue #19, marked TODO(#19) in discovery.ts.

nodes.label: graphify agent workflow
nodes.rationale: Codebase questions go to graphify query first; graph outputs are derived artifacts and must never be hand-edited. AST-only updates cost nothing, so they run after every code change.

nodes.label: fallow agent workflow
nodes.rationale: Every fallow command gets || true because exit 1 means "issues found" and only exit 2 is a real error. Deletions need a --trace confirmation first: fallow is syntactic, so an export can be imported-but-unreferenced and a dependency can be loaded by config rather than by import.

nodes.label: Comment conventions
nodes.rationale: Comments explain why rather than what, stay short, and mark incomplete work as TODO(WP-xxx). JSDoc on every exported function and type.

nodes.label: Triage label vocabulary
nodes.rationale: A canonical five-label set — needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix — so triage state is one axis.

nodes.label: GitHub issue tracker workflow
nodes.rationale: Issues and PRDs live as GitHub issues on magicspon/codedocs, driven entirely through the gh CLI, which infers the repo from git remote -v.

nodes.label: Wayfinder-to-GitHub mapping
nodes.rationale: Map is an issue labelled wayfinder:map, a ticket is a sub-issue labelled wayfinder:<type>, claiming is self-assignment, blocking uses GitHub's native dependencies, and the frontier is the open, unblocked, unassigned sub-issues.

nodes.label: Sub-issue and dependency API usage
nodes.rationale: Both APIs take the issue's database id, not its number, and need gh api -F (typed) rather than -f, which fails with a 422 "not of type integer". Issues must exist before they can reference each other, so create in one pass and wire in a second.

nodes.label: Research findings placement
nodes.rationale: No per-ticket research branch: parallel research agents share one working tree and cannot each check out a branch. Findings go to a distinct file under docs/research/ on the current branch, linked from the ticket's resolution comment.

nodes.label: cspell project word list
nodes.rationale: Holds the project's domain vocabulary — SCIP, LSIF, Kythe, calcom, callees, codegen, interner, graphify, fallowrc, wayfinder — so spellcheck can gate CI without false positives.

nodes.label: CI pipeline
nodes.rationale: Runs on pull requests into main with in-progress cancellation, pinning pnpm 11.22.0 and Node 24.19.0, then spellcheck, lint, typecheck and test as separate failing steps.

nodes.label: Node 24.19 requirement
nodes.rationale: Node 24.19 runs codedocs' TypeScript directly and provides node:sqlite, so there is no build step and no native module to compile. CI pins the same version the README requires.
